notes.title: Devlog #53
notes.content:
Hi everyone, it's time for our Friday devlog, although this is more like a Saturday devlog now, but let's keep the name the same! In this devlog, I'll explain in depth the current situation with crashes and what we're going to do about it.

Why all the lag & Crashes?

During launch, we saw an enormous amount of players and broke our previous all-time high player count by twofold. We had experience running highly populated servers in Korea, which is why we thought our servers could handle it, but they were still slowing down too much, more than we had anticipated. 

The main problem causing the servers to slow down was the way Unreal Engine handles replication (how the server decides what information to send to each player). The server CPU had to calculate the distance between every placeable and item that players had placed to all players, and figure out if they were close enough that the player needed to be sent that information. Our servers could have over 100,000 placed items, and when we had 80 players, for example, the calculations became so heavy that servers couldn't handle it effectively.

We found a couple of solutions and decided to try the "replication graph" method, which does the same thing as before but divides the map into a grid and performs calculations based on which grid the player is in. This solved the performance problem, and now all servers are running at least 10 ticks (calculations) per second. Unfortunately, the plugin that implements replicationgraph has some compatibility issues causing frequent random crashes. We managed to make it slightly better, but we're now in a situation where servers usually stay online for only about 3-4 hours.

What next?

I want to first apologize for the state the game is currently in. We acknowledge that a fully released game should not be in this condition. We will be doing a few things to resolve the issue:

1. We're trying to solve the crashes by fixing how Unreal Engine handles "bad" actors that are no longer in memory, which currently causes the crashes.

2. If we don't manage to fix it by next Wednesday, we'll revert to the old replication method and try alternative approaches until we have a stable 10-tick rate minimum and at least 12 hours of uptime on servers.

3. After this, we'll start focusing on all the bugs and issues which cause item and progression loss, as this is the most frustrating thing when playing in a persistent world where all items are hard to get.

On the bright side, our artists are working on new content updates currently planned for June and another in august with the next official server wipe. More information on these will come in next Friday's devlogs!

Thank you for your support, and again, apologies for the current state of the game.

- Sven

What's Happening Next?
As this episode of Longvinter's phase comes to an end, naturally a new one begins, and I know you will have quite a lot of new content to dig through this time. We will be focusing on making the game work great on Steam Deck with refined controller support on all the menus and also fixing bugs that come up with the new update. We also want to keep the performance at its best from here on out.

For our next big feature update, we already teased this but it is now confirmed that we will have Longvinter Farming coming as "1.1" version of the game. We have also planned a big overhaul to new player experience and introducing renting apartments and shared communities. More info on these coming later so as always stay tuned for more!

PlayStation Release Coming in 2026
I am also excited to announce that the game will be releasing on PlayStation next year! The game will provide cross-play options so we don't have two separate player bases limiting player numbers. 

New Tackle Catalog: Long Winter
Naturally when we didn't include any new catalog and tackle box last Christmas, it's now time to introduce a new set of winter clothing in style of the game's name. This is our biggest one yet, and we have some unique features like changing ski colors on backpacks and unique decals on mouth pieces. While this time there are no new effects, these items can drop with all of your favorite effects from the past!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/d141536c0e963d9e05a2b94216ef6f522cf1378b.png

1.0 Update Main Features
We wanted the 1.0 update to change something major in the game to really make it feel different for those who have played during Early Access. For that, we implemented new Points of Interest - Oil Rigs, which are large structures with significant verticality, quite challenging to design with our top-down game approach. Since this is our 1.0 update, we wanted to improve every aspect of the game, and we're really happy with how this update turned out. We have almost 100 new items with various mechanics. Let's start with the biggest change - the Oil Reworks.

Oil Rigs
If you visit Sgt. Lake now, you may notice that fuel prices have increased quite significantly since your last visit. That's because the LRI have set up oil rigs around the Longvinter archipelago and are now controlling prices everywhere. You must take destiny into your own hands and process and steal your own fuel while under attack from LRI mercenaries. These new locations are super fun for both PVP and PVE players, and we're excited to see what you like most about them! With the addition of fuel refining, we've added Crude Oil as a new item that needs to be refined before turning into fuel. We've also added a new upgrade tree to the mining rig building - instead of crushing rocks, you can now pump oil yourself and use refineries to bring your own product to the economy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/c2c54e5d1ba037c736971801ecd347a00f8d5f5e.png

Heli Crash and Underground Arena
Keeping in style of adding new interesting events, we have now added a heli crash to the map that lets you access new tactical gear that LRI use to try and hunt you down. We also have a new arena that invites all players every hour to fight to the last man in order to access the best loot right below Sgt. Lake base camp.

New Animals and Mounts
Our map now has much greater variety in animals with the introduction of Lynx, Wolf, Wolverine, Fox, Moose and Goats now wandering in Longvinter Island. All of the new animals are also obtainable as mounts, and we have made the saddles unequippable so you can style your mounts as you like it best.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/9e6e6a01ea3ad6a7429d91f163734642ae4a041d.png

Wildlife Improvements and Map Additions
New small birds have now been included in all parts of the map that bring the island alive with their amusing looks and ability to always escape you no matter how hard you try to catch them. With this amazing new atmospheric addition, we have also added new roads to help starting players travel around first outposts more easily. Vendor catalogs have been upgraded with many new items, and we've improved many other things visually and brought more animations to everything to make the world feel more alive and immersive.

We wanted to give placeable health more thought since it was previously a bit of an afterthought. Now we're really happy with new mechanics we have in place. You can see every placeable's health when hovering over them in inventory and while they're placed down. When you first place an item on the ground, they initially start with 31 HP and start gaining their health slowly. If a placeable takes damage, it will stop regenerating HP. notes.title: Devlog #52
notes.content:
Final Early Access Devlog

We're approaching a significant milestone as this will be our last devlog while the game is in Early Access. We want to express our deepest gratitude to all our players who have helped shape Longvinter into what it has become.

1.0 Wipe and Update Schedule
We're excited to announce that 1.0 will be releasing next Friday, February 21st, at 9AM UTC. All official servers will undergo a wipe immediately after the update goes live. We recommend unofficial servers to also perform a wipe if they experience any issues post-update.

We've finalized our wipe policy for official servers, implementing a 6-month wipe cycle (excluding monthly wipe servers). We believe this strikes the best balance between players who enjoy fresh starts and those who prefer persistent gameplay. To improve transparency, we've added a next wipe date display in the main menu while playing. This feature aims to prevent any unexpected surprises and keep our players informed about upcoming wipes. We want to remind everyone that hosting your own server allows you to maintain control over your saves and wipe schedule.

1.0 Experimental Recap
The new update has been thoroughly tested in our experimental branch, where our community has been instrumental in reporting issues. We've already addressed over 100 reported problems and are working to resolve all remaining issues before next Friday's release. From experience, we understand that some bugs may slip through to the stable version despite extensive testing, but we'll be working throughout the launch weekend to ensure the smoothest experience possible.

Steam Deck Compatibility
We're pleased to announce that with the 1.0 update, Longvinter will be fully playable on Steam Deck running the latest software version, with no workarounds required. We've verified this functionality on our own Steam Deck.

Prestige After Launch
We've received numerous inquiries about prestige retention after the 1.0 update. While we're aware that some players have achieved prestige levels through exploits, we've decided to preserve all prestige progress out of respect for those who earned it legitimately. We believe prestige represents a significant achievement for honest players, and we don't want to diminish their accomplishments. However, we want to remind everyone that the upcoming wipe will clear all Mk currency, so if you're planning to purchase prestige, we recommend doing so before next week's update.

Server Population Cap
After pushing our server capabilities to their limits, we've determined that a 100-player cap provides the optimal balance between performance and gameplay experience. This decision allows us to maintain server stability while still delivering an engaging multiplayer environment.

Looking Forward
We want to assure our community that reaching 1.0 is not the end of Longvinter's journey. Our development will continue, and we're excited to announce our future plans soon!

notes.title: Devlog #51
notes.content:
Happy New Year and welcome to this year's first devlog!

We're more excited than ever as the experimental version of the 1.0 update is nearly ready for public testing, and we can't wait to share what we've been developing over the past 6 months. Experimental patch notes and discussions will take place in our Discord server, so be sure to join and get yourself an "experimental-tester" role to be notified when the update is ready for testing. While experimental patch notes will be shared in Discord, the final notes will be available here when the game launches with wipe and the update goes live on all servers on February 21, 2025.

We've moved the release date three days earlier to Friday (instead of Monday) to give everyone time to play during the weekend. The 1.0 update will remain in an experimental state for almost a month, giving us enough time to polish it into what we're proud to call a fully released game.

Let's go over some of the changes we've been working on:

Placeable Health Changes
We wanted to make raiding during active gameplay a more viable option. Since placeable health has been somewhat of an afterthought, we've now given it the polish required to enable fun raiding gameplay. Changes primarily affect building under fire - in 1.0, placed items will start with only 30 HP and slowly regenerate to full health after placement. Additionally, recently damaged items cannot be picked up and replaced, and items that haven't fully regenerated their health won't drop as bags when destroyed, preventing players from repeatedly using the same items as cover.

Bullet Sync Issues
We've addressed an ongoing issue where bullets visible on your screen weren't hitting their displayed locations. This "lag" occurred because bullets began their journey before reaching the server, which was intended to provide instant feedback. Without delving too deeply into technical details, we've implemented server-side lag compensation, resulting in much more responsive shooting mechanics. We've recorded comparison videos showing this issue in the current beta 1.14 build versus the new lag-compensated bullets in the 1.0 build. While other players' bullets may occasionally appear to spawn slightly after their gun barrel, we believe this trade-off is worthwhile for improved accuracy when leading shots.

New Dances Coming in Tackle Box

notes.title: Devlog #49
notes.content:
Hi everyone! Hope you all have been able to get a chance at catching and getting back at the clown that has been causing mayhem in the server by stealing items. We have exciting news for you all. Longvinter now has a release date for its 1.0 update, and we also have a question about wipes that we want to ask opinions about.

Release Date for 1.0 Update

We have decided not to rush the update since we have so many new things planned for it, and we want to make it meaningful enough for all players who have already played Longvinter to try it out again and return to play. This is why we have decided to launch the 1.0 update next year on the same date that we originally launched in early access, which is February 24, 2025! This update will come with a wipe since we have made substantial changes to the economy of the fuel, and then everyone will get a chance to experience Longvinter as we would have wanted it to be experienced 3 years ago!

We are aware of Steam Deck issues, but currently, we cannot reproduce the problem on our own deck, which has slowed down the troubleshooting greatly. We will look into it more next week and try to figure out what's wrong with it! Sorry for the issue taking so long to resolve.

Should We Wipe Before Christmas?

Many players in our Discord have been asking about the wipe day, and we're considering the possibility of a wipe before next year, given that the full release is still quite far off. We want to hear from you! We'll be creating a survey soon where you can voice your opinion on whether you'd prefer a wipe at the start of December or to continue playing without interruption until the full release.

Importantly, we'll be gathering opinions from each region individually. For example, if the Asia region wants a wipe but the EU region doesn't, we'll only wipe the Asia servers in December. This approach allows us to cater to the preferences of different player communities.

We encourage you to participate in the upcoming survey to help us make this decision. In the meantime, feel free to share your thoughts on wipes in general in the comments below. Your feedback is crucial in shaping the Longvinter experience for everyone!

notes.title: Devlog #48
notes.content:
Hi everyone! It's been a while since our last devlog, so let's catch up on what the team has been working on. With summer vacations wrapping up for our employees, we're back in full swing, building the next update. We also released a trailer for a new game, which is super exciting! We'd like to clarify some things people have been discussing, so let's dive in.

New Update Taking Shape

The new oil rig environments are starting to look ready, although they're still missing some new props. We wanted these areas to have puzzles and enemy NPCs like the mines, so they've taken quite a lot of time for 3D modeling and level design. Here's an update video showcasing one of the three new oil rig locations we're cooking up:

[previewyoutube=ilfgg-JlnSQ;full][Update video][/previewyoutube]

We're also preparing to add three vests you can wear in the game. These will give you quick access to certain items in your inventory without opening it. For example, we're planning a reload vest that lets you reload by just pressing an action button, automatically loading ammo from your inventory into your weapon.

For those wondering, the next update will come with a wipe because we're making big changes to fuel and want the economy on servers to start fresh with these new changes.

Autumn Tackle Box

We're still figuring out how to get everything ready before the next update. We're considering limiting the autumn tackle box to a small collection of items or possibly skipping the box for now and focusing on adding things to a future update.

Longvinter Leaving Early Access

That's right! Some of you may have put two and two together and realized that as we prepare to launch a new game, we're also finally leaving Early Access. We know the game isn't bug-free, but we've achieved a lot with server performance. The game is in a completely different state compared to when we first launched.

The game's various mechanics, items, and systems working together have created an environment where small changes can break things in unexpected places. This has been a big project for our small team, but we've learned a lot. We'll continue ironing out issues and bring you the most stable Longvinter experience yet with the full release.

There are still problems with containers not spawning after server restarts, but we've been steadily fixing issues and will continue to do so in the future. We haven't wiped the servers in almost three months, so some problems are just now showing up since we haven't run servers without a wipe for this long.

What's After Early Access?

We've already planned at least two more content updates for the game after the official launch, so don't worry – there will be plenty of new things to experience on Longvinter island! We've completed all the features we made public in our first roadmap last year, and we'll continue developing new content.

After oil rigs, new mounts, and animals are in the game, we're planning a full farming update with a new buildable barn and tameable animals. We're excited to share more info when we have the details ready. We also want to add more endgame content for our dedicated players who speedrun the game's compendium and other features.

We're reading your suggestions on Discord and adding suitable ideas to our progress tracker for future implementation. There's sometimes a big time frame between adding a suggestion and deciding whether to include it in a future update, but we read all of them and will continue to do so. Keep the suggestions coming!

Thank you, and see you all on Longvinter island!

New update is in the works

We're thrilled with the server performance improvements achieved in the 1.14 update. Seeing 150 players simultaneously on the KR 5 server was a remarkable milestone, surpassing the goal of 100-player servers that we set when we launched in Early Access.

Currently, we're focusing on two major aspects:

If you upgraded your prestige and want to move over to another server, there is currently a bug in the game that prevents you from obtaining the upgrade on another server. You can easily fix this by deleting your preferences save file, which causes prestige to be resynced with your device, fixing the problem.

Go to C:\Users\username\AppData\Local\Longvinter\Saved\SaveGames and delete the preferences.sav file. Then, when you log back into the game, it should give you the prestige.

Introducing the hardcore server

We've been planning a new server concept that offers a unique Longvinter experience, tailored for players seeking a more challenging and rewarding gameplay. This dedicated server will accommodate up to 200 players, depending on performance.

The hardcore server is designed for players who enjoy a more punishing and intense playstyle. Here are the currently proposed "rule" changes for the hardcore server (subject to change):


 No code locks on houses or tents
 Turrets can be destroyed
 Players drop half their currency on death

notes.title: Devlog #45
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 🙋‍♀️🙋‍♂️

Spring has been starting super slow here in Finland, and we just received a fresh coat of snow here in Helsinki. But time goes forward nonetheless, and we have just finished the feature list for 1.14. Those can be read on our roadmap on Trello. We will be updating the progress on those in real-time so you know when to expect the new update.

Last week for tackle boxes

Spring tackle boxes have been dropping now for over a month. We have decided to stop the drops for the tackle boxes in a week, so you will have until May 6th to get tackle boxes from playing the game. We will be increasing the drop window for tackle boxes from a 2-day cooldown to a 1-day cooldown. For the rest of the month and the first week of next month, you can get a tackle box by logging in every day!

1.14 feature list

As we discussed in an earlier devlog, we now focus more on quality of life and gameplay-related changes, not new features. I would like to highlight a couple of things here, but the full list of planned changes can be read on our Trello page.


 Decay time increase
We want to allow players to keep their houses for longer with minimal maintenance. For this, we plan to add a new upgrade to the LRI stations where you can buy an upgrade that extends your house decay time for another week. We feel that since servers have quite a lot of room for houses now, and introducing motors to boats has shrunk the size and made areas more accessible, we can allow players to keep their houses for longer.

 Normal stones can be broken with a pickaxe
This will be a small change but allows many more options to build your house.

 More dice games
We plan to have more dice games finally implemented, and we would love to hear your suggestions on simple but engaging table games that can be played with dice to be implemented.


EU server reset and KR1 placeable data loss

Unfortunately, we had a couple of incidents with the servers where errors filled up the drives of the machine unexpectedly. This resulted in the server not saving items on the server correctly or not at all. We have taken measures to clear up the server files that take too much space, and we have acquired a new backup server where we will be backing up all the saves periodically so we have the saves on at least 2 machines at all times.

Thank you for reading and come say hi to us in Discord!

notes.title: Devlog #44
notes.content:
Good Friday to everyone! 😊

It's been so nice seeing many of you trying out the new update and coming back to the game. I hope you have enjoyed your time on the Longvinter island. If you haven't tried the new update yet, you can still play this weekend and get an Easter bunny drop. The drops will stop on Monday, so this is your last chance!

What is coming moving forward

The next major update (1.14) will not focus on adding any new major features but rather on refining and fixing the current game to a much better state. 
We have prioritized adding new things over fixing existing issues because we didn't want to fix everything only for it to break again after the next update. However, we now feel that it's a good moment to pause for a second and thoroughly go through all aspects of the game to make changes that will improve it. But don't worry, we will be planning and creating new assets constantly to have a big update after 1.14! 

Update 1.14 will also have some new features that can be easily implemented but have a big impact. We will go over these in more detail in the coming Friday Devlogs.

New features

What's New in 1.13

Customization

We're excited to build upon the new item system introduced in the 1.12 update. This system offers us greater flexibility in game code, and we're ready to leverage its full potential in the next update, starting with boat customization. You'll soon be able to personalize your dinghies, equip them with motors and storage boxes, and even color them in one of seven unique shades!

We're also working on customizable weapon attachments, which will alter your weapon's handling, damage, spread, bullet velocity, and laser aiming.

Moreover, we're introducing a coloring station where you can use paints (also a new addition in the upcoming update) to color all new placeable items in seven vibrant hues currently offered partially in the Allotment garden set. Here are the colors we have planned: White, Charcoal, Blue, Red, Yellow, Mint, and Blush.

New House Upgrades

We're also eager to expand the upgrade options for the new cabin. The planned upgrades will provide players with more advantages than just an ordinary cabin, but won't include code lock protection, making all stored items vulnerable to raids by other players. This is part of our strategy to balance gameplay between those who enjoy raiding and those who prefer the existing system. All new upgrades will necessitate at least one cabin placed on the map before other structures can be added.

Water Mill - A water-based upgrade featuring a waterwheel for power generation and storage. (Raidable)

Storefront/Trading Post - An extension of the vending machine offering more role-play and player engagement opportunities. This upgrade will also come with an overhaul of the cooking system, introducing status effects for complex recipes. (Not raidable)

Gallery - An accessible building where players can display their prized trophies and items. (Raidable)

Mining Rig - Extract ores from the ground. (Raidable)

Spring Biome

As we approach summer, we're also bringing Spring to Longvinter Island in the next update. Spring will introduce its own art style, a new wood type, and a unique flower to the biome.

notes.title: 1.11 Halloween update
notes.content:
Changes

Added 10 new cosmetic items to the game that can be earned by playing the game during the Halloween event. Note that some rewards must be discovered from the game level to unlock them.

Optimized player turrets to not be as CPU intensive on the server side
Mining helmet can now be bought from the vendor in Sgt. Lake base camp
Electric pickaxe can now be found in weapon chests
Trees can now spawn a maximum of 7 wood & 2 resin when chopped


Weapon balance changes
Semi-automatic, Submachine gun and chainsaw are the most popular weapons with 85% of all kills made by these 3 weapons. With this update, we wanted to tune down these a bit and make other 
weapons more serious options.


Semi-automatic

Semi-auto has been the most popular weapon by a long shot due to its easy acquisition compared to other weapons and its constant damage output. We wanted to emphasize its role as Marskman weapon with the following changes:
Increased the damage from 9 → 12
Reduced fire rate by 33%

Chainsaw

While we want to keep the relevance of a melee weapon in the game we thought that chainsaw was a bit too good. We wanted to lower movement speed to prevent chasing but changed the fire rate/damage ratio to keep it more constant
Lowered movement speed while “firing” by 10%
Increased fire rate by 100%
Decreased damage from 16 → 7

Submachine gun

The submachine gun was also trendy and the global average kill distance was so short that it seems obvious why submachine gun and chainsaw both dominated the place for most used weapon. We wanted to keep its relevancy as the top close combat weapon but we felt like its 1,5-second TTK was too little to allow an opponent to react when shot
Reduced fire rate by 25%



Some other weapons were really lacking in damage or fire rate department and we wanted to raise some weapons stats to be better at their intended role

Crossbow

Crossbow was when introduced intended to be an easy to acquire hunting and combat tool. The current damage was just not cutting it in combat or when hunting and we wanted to give it a serious damage buff to make it shine. Although it will still be a bit lacking with projectile speed and reload speed this should give it more roles as a finisher or when playing in a group and bursting down enemies
Increased damage from 10 → 30

Shotgun

The shotgun is also another early-game weapon really just lacks damage and we wanted to give a little damage boost to make it more in line with other weapons and allow you to do more than just hunting with it
Increased pellet damage from 3.33 → 4 (Note that the shotgun shoots 6 pellets so total single-shot damage is now 20)

Auto shotgun

Automatic shotgun was always meant to be really deadly in close to mid-range but it really did not live up to its intended purpose. Here are the changes we are making to the weapon in order to make it compete with submachine gun as the ultimate close combat weapon that uses more ammo and is not as versatile
Increased pellet damage from 2.5 → 3.5(This shotgun has also 6 pellets per shot)
Increased the ammo consumption/shot from 6 to 12

To make it more punishing to miss your shot and to make this a premium option

Damage fall of increased by 400%

This ensures the intended role as a close combat weapon

Increased fire rate by 50%

Makes the time to kill in line with the submachine gun

Upcoming Seasonal Events
With summer now behind us, we sense the bubbling anticipation for Halloween and other festive events to make their mark in the game! We've been cooking up some fresh item drops for you. And don’t forget—there’s just one more week left in our building contest. If you haven’t submitted your creative endeavours, fill out the submission form soon! Upcoming Weapon balance update
You might have noticed the new EULA, which mentions that we are now collecting data on player behavior and other in-game activities. We’re using this data to gain insights into various game dynamics, especially focusing on identifying any imbalances. Based on our findings, we’re gearing up to roll out our first balance update soon, aiming to particularly address disparities in weapon balance that we’ve observed. Rest assured, our intent with this data collection is solely to enhance game balance and overall player experience! Keep an eye out for more updates on upcoming improvements.


1.12 & Revamped Item System
We've been listening to feedback and recognize the need for a deeper, more interactive cooking experience. With the upcoming 1.12 update, we're bringing you just that.

Previously, the scope for culinary creativity was limited. Next, in the 1.12 update, players will have the freedom to mix and match ingredients. The resulting dish will possess unique attributes and appearances, reflecting the components used. For instance, incorporating chilli into a recipe will bestow a heat buff, similar to some current dishes. Moreover, the energy value of a dish will vary based on the ingredients and their quantities. As an example, cooking a dish using three fishes will pack more energy than one made with a single fish, allowing players to optimize inventory space with nutrient-rich food.

To achieve this culinary evolution, we're undertaking a significant overhaul of the entire item system, rebuilding it from the ground up. This foundation will enhance the cooking experience and pave the way for numerous exciting features. With the capability to assign custom values to any item in the inventory, we can now introduce nuances like varying weights for fish, weapon attachments, and customizable placeables.

However, a significant change of this magnitude means that all current inventories will be reset to align with the new system. We understand this may be inconvenient, but it's a necessary step to usher in this game-enhancing update. Major new features

This can be obtained by doing the compendium tasks eg. fishing, farming and hunting. The chance of dropping one is really small but when you get one, you can exchange it to the mount with each of the compendium vendors. 

Once you have equipped the wolf, you cannot lose it to death.

notes.title: Devlog #35
notes.content:
Welcome to Friday Devlog!

Modding Support

The final version of our modding support is now ready and we're planning to distribute it gradually through Google Forms submissions. Just fill out the form and we will give access to the GitHub repository.

What Can You Achieve with Modding?

To begin, you'll need the source build Unreal Engine 4.26 to access the project editor. We've made specific elements modifiable by adding a "replaceable actor" component to the items you're permitted to modify. Here's an overview of what you can currently achieve with modding:

- Introduce new items to the game, such as food, plants, weapons, and additional placeable objects for your house
- Customize homes with varying appearances and colors, or upgrade turrets instead of electrical systems, and more
- Create new in-game events, like air drops
- Make alterations to Longvinter Island; while custom maps are not yet functional, you can still manipulate the map by spawning objects and executing server code
- Modify the player character by adjusting running speed, enabling a fully rotatable camera, and adding custom character models. Since we use the Unreal Engine's default mannequin character skeleton, you can easily introduce new models as player characters, as well as custom UI elements
- Replace chests to offer improved loot or increased quantities of existing loot

As someone who has spent countless hours modding games like Skyrim and Fallout, I'm thrilled to see what unique creations you'll produce with our modding tools. We'll review your ideas submitted through the forms and create guided tutorials for the most popular ones, helping you get started as quickly as possible! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/9da4876bd6c208213f2c531ab2aa673e797c9fa9.png

When is the next update arriving?

Before we release the next major update, we'll first apply a hotfix to address the remaining issues and ensure that modding support functions smoothly. This will also resolve any critical bugs still present in the game. Following that, we'll start working on the forthcoming update, which will prioritize your feedback, implement quality of life enhancements, and incorporate your suggestions.

We've already begun developing features like customizable chest names and the ability to quickly sort items within chests by value, rarity, and category. Additionally, we'll be introducing the highly anticipated and previously postponed hostile wolf to the game. As we finalize our objectives for this update, we'll share more details about the planned changes. Furthermore, we will continue to work on fixing bugs and incorporating the quality of life improvements you've recommended.

We appreciate the feedback and input from our players and are committed to providing the best possible gaming experience for all. Thank you for your continued support!

notes.title: Devlog #34
notes.content:
Welcome to Friday Devlog!

Modding support

We made every effort to have modding support ready for the launch of this update, but unfortunately, we couldn't complete all the desired features. We also didn't want to delay the update any further, as server progress was wiped due to update requirements. We saw that many players were eagerly awaiting the wipe more than the update itself. We apologize for the issues encountered at launch and are working diligently to address them. In the coming weeks, we'll be resolving the remaining significant issues and adding modding support. Let's also address some other concerns that have been raised. In the meantime, we encourage players to start preparing by installing the required source build of Unreal Engine 4.26. We appreciate your patience and understanding as we continue to work towards delivering the best possible gameplay experience for our community.


Currently known issues

We've received reports of a bug that emerged since introducing controller support. This issue causes characters to halt their movement when eating or interacting with items in the inventory. We have already taken steps to mitigate this problem and will continue working to resolve all instances where it occurs.

Another significant concern you've shared is related to gun recoil while moving. In version 1.10b, we transitioned to a new character model using Unreal Engine's skeleton, simplifying the animation process. Previously, movement recoil was solely managed through animation. We decided to switch to a random spread calculation for better control over recoil. While we intend to maintain a slight accuracy reduction when moving to give retreating players a better chance of survival, we plan to adjust the recoil next week. We'll closely monitor your feedback and continue fine-tuning until we reach a satisfactory balance for all players.

Results of Player Survey on Official Server Wipes

Recently, we conducted a survey to gather feedback from players on server wipes. We received 197 responses, and here are the key results regarding the server wipes:

Do you want all official servers to have wipes?

Yes: 54.8%
No: 45.2%

Would you rather have:

All official servers wiped: 38.1%
All PVP and monthly wipe servers wiped: 9.1%
All PVE and monthly wipe servers wiped: 16.2%
Only separate monthly wipe servers: 36.5%

How often should the Normal servers be wiped?

Every month: 18.6%
Every 3 months: 41.5%
Every 6 months: 39.8%

After analyzing the results of the player survey, we are thinking about making some changes to our wipe policy. We would be keeping the Monthly wipe servers, which will reset every month, and we would be wiping the other official servers every 6 months.

We believe that this approach strikes a good balance between the desires of our player base and the need to maintain a stable and fair gaming environment. Players who enjoy the frequent reset of progress and the challenge of starting fresh can continue to play on the Monthly wipe servers, while those who prefer a longer-term experience can enjoy the other official servers.

We appreciate the feedback and input from our players and are committed to providing the best possible gaming experience for all. Thank you for your continued support!

Scheduled Wipe and Update in Two Weeks

The upcoming update will necessitate a complete wipe on official servers, as we plan to expand the available house building area and modify the number of houses a player can place. The scheduled update and wipe will take place on April 13, 2023.

Enhanced Modding Support and Update 1.10b

Although we haven't tested the newly optimized build yet, we are optimistic about its performance following the update. Additionally, we have refactored portions of the code to enhance security and reduce the risk of hacking.

Integration of AMD FidelityFX™ Super Resolution

In our next update, we will be incorporating FSR support, significantly boosting frame rates for players who have struggled to achieve a stable 60 fps. FSR technology renders the game at a lower resolution before upscaling the image, making it compatible with all devices and a prime choice for implementation.

Greetings! The team has been working hard to bring you the next big update for Longvinter. I am thrilled to share all the exciting new content and improvements with you. Uuvana and other projects

These changes would result in all mods becoming incompatible and needing to be updated. We apologize for the inconvenience, but this is a necessary step to ensure a secure and stable gaming experience for everyone. After we release the 1.10 update, we will focus on improving performance and fixing bugs in the 1.10b build, which will finally include the modding support.

notes.title: Devlog #29
notes.content:
This is the first devlog of 2023. Happy New Year, everyone! We hope that you had a wonderful holiday season and are ready to take on the new year with renewed energy and excitement.

We're hard at work on the new update and we can't wait to share some new details with you!

Asian server wipes

We understand that the decision to wipe the Asian server may have caused some disappointment for our players. However, we felt it was necessary in order to address the significant lag issues caused by duplication glitches that were being exploited by some players. These glitches allowed a small number of players to acquire large amounts of in-game currency, which created an unfair advantage and negatively impacted the overall gaming experience for others. We have now taken steps to fix these bugs and believe that wiping the server is the most effective solution to improve performance. It's important to note that unofficial servers are not affected by this decision. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your understanding as we work to improve the overall quality of the game.

Next update

We're excited to share some of the new features and improvements that will be included in our upcoming update. While we can't give a specific release date just yet, we want to give you a better understanding of the progress we've made and what still needs to be done before the update is ready to be rolled out. Here are some of the new things you can expect to see in the next update:

New weapons

The long-awaited machine gun is finally coming, as well as three additional weapons will be included in the next update. While the models for all four weapons are complete, the crossbow will require the addition of a new ammo type before it can be added to the game. In the meantime, here are some preview images of all the new weapons to whet your appetite!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/f5bc2be63e2093d6740cf8b7f5ac08e24629a3c6.png

Disassembly machine

Are you tired of being stuck without the necessary components to craft your desired weapons? We have some exciting news for you! The next update will introduce the ability to disassemble other weapons that are crafted with Long Gun Barrels via the new Disassembly machine, giving you the option to obtain the parts you need without ever leaving the house. The machine uses electricity so you need to plan accordingly. You can dismantle anything that is crafted with this machine, there is a small chance that some components are lost during the dismantling process. Only the model is ready so we still need to implement interaction.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/f76325b996ad5c71dec3bd44b2414cc5bdbc0ee4.png

Advanced workbench

The upcoming update will introduce the advanced workbench, which will enhance the crafting system by increasing the number of required components for certain items. This change may make obtaining some items take more time, but it also allows us to better distinguish between early-game and late-game items by still utilizing basic crafting materials such as wood and metal parts. This will create a more nuanced and engaging crafting experience for players, allowing for a greater sense of progression and accomplishment as they progress through the game. For this one as well only the model is ready so we still need to implement interaction.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/f6131896f685bd0b233794235f867cb8745dbba4.png

Modding support

In the upcoming update, we will be releasing a portion of the game's source code, allowing the community to create their own mods using Unreal Engine. This is a huge step forward for us and we can't wait to see the creative and innovative mods the community will create. To facilitate this, we will be releasing full modding tutorials and adding a dedicated tab for modded servers in the server browser. Additionally, we have already made progress in implementing a modding package manager, and we're currently working on figuring out the best way to handle installation and integration with Steam Workshop. This is an exciting time for the community and we look forward to seeing the new possibilities and experiences that mods will bring to the game.

Controller support

We are excited to announce that controller support is finally coming to Longvinter, a feature that our players have been requesting since the game's launch. With this update, players will have the option to play the game in a more relaxed and comfortable way. We understand that controller support is important to many players, and we're glad to be able to make this feature a reality.

Quality of life over content

Weekly wipe servers to monthly wipe

notes.title: Recap of last update and removal of discord support ticket system
notes.content:
Laggy servers

The last update introduced unexpected lag and many problems to those who had updated their house interior. We tried to fix the object pop stutters and memory leaks by cooking the peaceable class so that it was faster to load in memory but took more space in memory. We thought this was fine because there were only about 100 max placeables on screen simultaneously. But this issue came up when running on the full server where each player used around 50% more memory on a server than previously and the server executable would eat 20 Gb of memory on the fully populated server. And because of this official Korean servers 1-3 lost their house placement data when we closed the servers to update them. We are sorry this happened and we will continue optimizing servers as we move towards bigger maps that require more computing power to run more AI and houses etc.

New way to contact us about longvinter
As of today, we are moving away from the Discord ticket system. Discord will still be used as a place to talk about the game, get help from the community and report bugs and meet new people. Press, Business, Hacker, abusive player and technical support reports will be done by filling the form in contact.uuvana.com and communicating by email.

notes.title: Friday Devlog #20
notes.content:
20 devlogs released already. Time flies so fast and I'm so proud to look back on how far we have come.

Since the game was released we have doubled the item count in the game. Added electricity and other upgrade options to the tents. Character customization, quests, teams, and other great features that have really improved the game and made it already a much smoother experience.

This week's devlog will still be quite dry in terms of images but I am sure next time I have some nice concrete things to show you.

Next official server wipe

The next official server wipe will be on 19.8.2022. 

Boats and bigger map

We feel like now is the right time to make the map bigger and finally try to stop wiping progression. We have already finished the layout of the map expansion. This will have the same islands that are currently present on the map but we are adding new islands around them. There will be a total of 10 new islands that can be explored. Also, a number of smaller islands are added to go alongside new boats.

All the compendium vendors are moving away from Sgt. Lake base camp and are given their own islands. These islands will require you to complete half of the compendium in order to enter the area and they will have some activities related to the compendium.

Bunkers and enemies

We want to make the looting areas more interesting and we are adding underground bunkers that can be accessed by an elevator that is found inside the buildings in POI

We have also been preparing to introduce hostile NPCs to the game to make PVE more interesting. When combining both the new underground parts for the point of interest and enemy NPCs, we need to rethink how loot is distributed over different areas and there will be changes to them as well. Currently finding weapons is far easier than finding parts and crafting them. Weapon drops will become much rarer and we keep the weapon part drops the same.

When next update is relased?

We currently don't want to give any exact date on when the next update is released. But when we update new things to experimental it usually takes 2 weeks to iron out all the issues that come up from experimental.

Dynamic vendor prices

We wanted the game to feel more like a multiplayer game where player interactions have even more impact on the world around them. In today's update, we re-enabled the Vendor dynamic prices. This system has two main components one that changes prices randomly over time and the second which is affected by what is sold to a vendor and bought from a vendor. 

For example, if all the players are selling common pike fish to a single vendor its price will drop to a minimum of 50% of the original price. This will force people to either stash their fish and wait for a price to go back up and then sell in bulk. Or the player can try to find another vendor that buys the item for a better price.

Teo

You'll have to start updating your community-made maps soon because there's a new island coming most likely next week, called "Isla Inocentes". it's horizontally as large as the mainland but vertically much slimmer. notes.title: Friday Devlog #7
notes.content:
Hey there! We've officially launched on Early Access, yay! It's been a hectic 24 hours, to say the least! 

First of all, we would like to thank those of you who bought the game. You guys have enabled us to continue on working this little game of ours and make it into the game we always wanted to make. We promise to keep you updated on every little thing we do on Discord. You can DM us directly or chat with us and our community members on the various channels we have, like #-suggestions and #-bugs-and-issues.

Here are some of the fixes we made on launch day:
- fixed vendor catalog getting messed up (caused by the vendor price fluctuation)
- added placeholder water for DirectX11 players
- fixed a crafting dupe
- fixed boat travel consistently causing players to lose their camera or fall into the void

- removed the old options menu and replaced it with the advanced options menu

- lowered actor network relevancy distances to try to alleviate the lag
- mezereon bushes grew cloudberries, not anymore
- fixed multiple spots on the map where the player could get stuck
- increased the hint text size
- fixed light posts flickering on dusk and dawn
- removed a couple of unfinished vendor locations
- fixed spots on the level where players got stuck easily
- fixed Poppy flower grow time
- fixed cooking book recipe requirements

One thing that really rubbed players the wrong way, and rightfully so, is the lag on official servers, and more specifically high population official servers. This is the biggest problem we wanted to solve with Early Access. We've started working on it already and what we've found is that we have a lot of actors, mostly "A_Item" actors that include flowers and bushes, that do not need to be replicated most of the time. So that's one thing, and I'm sure we'll find more actors like that next week!

After we fix the lag on the servers we'll move on to content updates! Here's what we have planned:
- PVE servers: Players can only kill each other only at points of interest in the north!
- More interior placeables
- More exterior placeables
- Expanded farming. More plants and every plant has a specific purpose and growing preference
- More variation in character looks
- New points of interest: Docks, North airport
- Compendium Guilds: Locked areas accessible only if you've completed the compendium list for that area

All in all, this was a successful launch and we're trying to make sure the first weekend goes smoothly!

Again, thank you for supporting the development, we'll keep you updated!
Teo & Nilsson

We did have the hangars and random containers here and there, but they were boring and outdated, and they will eventually be replaced by new, better-quality areas.

These warehouses I worked on this week are the first step in making the POIs more interesting. They are a mid-size building with varying amounts of loot. In the coming weeks, I'll be adding more buildings sizes that share the same theme as the warehouses you see here, and Nilsson will start placing them around and creating the actual POI areas!

[previewyoutube=ZtknUBG-CUs;full][/previewyoutube]

Lot of UI additions 
Nilsson

This week I focused on UI to finish up all the prepared mechanics that are now ready for testing.

New UI for status effects
I wanted the buff effect UI to the same standard that we have on all others.
For a recap, the buff is a temporary or permanent status effect on your character that affects certain actions. For example, Blackberry jam reduces incoming damage, and Rasberry jam makes you take less damage when you walk on snow.

You can also view additional information about the topic when you hover your mouse cursor over the icon longer.

This week I implemented the latter. Every time you walk by the bush a rare type of bird can jump out and you better try to catch it because good loot is just waiting for takers.

notes.title: Friday Devlog #2
notes.content:
This week's devlog is a little light in terms of new content since both of us had to be away from home for a couple of days, but don't worry, I'll be working through the weekend which means that in the next week's devlog we'll see more new content added!

I'll most probably work on the village placeable set this weekend, which I promised last week, so that is something you can expect to see next week! :)

 Please, join us on our Discord if you'd like to discuss game changes and additions. All feedback is welcome!
- Teo

Boat Travel 
Teo
You can now fast travel between outposts and other locations via interacting with the new boat that is located in multiple different outposts around the map.

You can travel to your starter outpost, which is tied to your SteamID free of charge, but all the other locations cost X amount of MK. Traveling to the WIP location called 'Hamari Village' will cost the least amount of MK of all available locations, since we want this to be a central hub where players can find their friends, get help and tools, and socialize.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/4fc9b4694a601f0a6cadc9762d436bd3c032105e.png

Every available location displays the following information on the 'Boat Travel' window:

 Location name
 Available services
 PVP / Safe, turret protected
 Coordinates
 Is the location in the snow
 Price

Use this new feature to travel according to your wealth. When you know you enough MK to buy new tools for better money-making methods, find out the vendor which has those tools for sale and that buys the resources you gather with the tool and travel to it!

Swimming Animations 
Nilsson

We have the game finally at the stage where we can start to give some love to features that have been the same as when Teo first created them one year ago. Swimming never had its own animation but the player character would just walk in the water. In my opinion, this worked surprisingly well but it's was now time to create dedicated swimming animations. 

Animations are created inside the engine to make it easier for implementation. Teo also added some nice sound effects. Check out the quick video below.

[previewyoutube=zLW87NKkWVE;full][/previewyoutube]

Chat command: /Roll 
Teo
Players can now generate a random number between two integers, by default 1-100. This is useful if a member of a group of equal players wants to claim something—such as a chest or a rare plant—they will roll for it.

Players can roll a random number using the following slash commands:

"/roll" returns a number between 1 and 100.
"/roll 50-200" returns a number between given min. and max. values, in this example 50-200.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/16611ccd8f3de3a142b5896f39069562ad2cdbf2.png

Getting Started Guide 
Teo
Since there is no info anywhere on what you should do in Longvinter, I added a new button in the main menu for beginners that opens a window that tells you what to do to get started in the game. Will be updated frequently to match the questions and problems players will have once we have more people playing the game!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/e29b87c593fecc8dfa015bef208f4134fda54819.png

Quality of Life & Localization 
Nilsson
During this week I focused a bit more on playing the game and finding different problems and bugs. We had a bug where one of the functions that were responsible for switching the player stance when the player started aiming was not set as network reliable and this caused the gun models to flicker and not be set visible. 

There were a number of other bugs fixed, see the list below!

Fixed bugs

When the player unequipped the fishing rod after catching the fish the fishing rod would reappear in the player's backpack unintentionally.
The bird AI would not reset its walking destination after it had been killed. This would cause the bird to walk in weird locations after it respawned. Fixed this by resetting the target destination after respawn.
Fixed a bug where inventory would become unresponsive if you would right-click(drop) item in the crafting menu.
Sometimes player would shoot itself if the network connection was bad.

Localization support!

The Unreal Engine has a simple built-in feature for detecting translatable text in-game, which enables us to add different cultures from translators. I just had to convert a couple of item names to use the "Text" variable and this auto-generated the files that can be used to fill in translations. If you are interested in translating the game texts for your native language please contact us in Discord!

Other changes

 Added a new SMG
 Projectiles now have damage drop off depending on the weapon

notes.content:
We are going to start posting weekly or bi-weekly progress updates called the 'Friday Devlog'* to be more open and accountable for the progress of Longvinter and to create an archive that anyone in the future could go back and look at.

*We'll try to keep these posts as regular as we can, but some variation on date and time each week is to be expected!

- Teo

Tent Upgrade: Cabins 
Teo

Come Early Access, you can now make real villages with your friends because this week I added the ability to upgrade the research tent into a cabin by depositing wood into a workbench. This is supposed to be a medium-length, early-game grind. Thanks for the suggestion, Jasmin!

There are 5 different colorways:

 Baby blue
 Blush
 Mint (a personal favorite)
 Lemon
 Barn red

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/c475d274c62a9d93ab83182812eaed2b689e7e24.png

This new addition of cabins required me to go back to one of the first features I made almost exactly a year ago which was the placeable tents. I removed the random rotation which was applied when you place down the tent. Instead, tents (and other placeables in the future) now have 'restricted rotation', meaning that you can only rotate the placable 22.5 degrees on each side. This way you won't have houses that face the wrong way from the players' perspective.

I saw a picture of a place called 'Brändaholm', a community garden by the sea in South-Sweden which has a bunch of cute houses next to each other and those were my main inspiration for the color and detail of the cabins. Making the models took me well over a day to make and adjusting colors and adding detail took a couple of hours on top of that.

You can also share the door code with your friends if you want to have friends over, but that I haven't implemented fully YET! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/1bfce96e29c756e2b81c162dc650873b663ddd0e.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/a1f956e7cf701e5388f8e912c66e964034168b71.png
The interior model is still WIP!

In the coming weeks before the Early Access release, I'm going to make an allotment garden/village placeable set that matches the aesthetic of the cabins. It will have stylized fences, a bench, an old-school village lamp post, and a garden table + chair set.

Sitting 
Nilsson

I was asked by Teo to make a sitting animation and logic for the player character. The process was relatively easy and the results are awesome and cute 🥰 This was also suggested by Jasmin, so thank you!
The current input for sittings is bound to the "X"  key.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/b82988d0616e0ba0debd51af3bc1a8a11a90562d.jpg

Buffs
Nilsson

To make items have more meaning in the game than just giving health or placing we wanted to make a status effect/buff system.

When the player consumes an item it gives the player a temporary status effect that is displayed on the HUD, UI is still WIP. The effect can give the player resistance to cold or make the player run faster. 

We will also implement this system to hats, which will give permanent effects that last as long as you have the item equipped.

New Items!
Nilsson

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40655015/05d135ffd725bfa704fe52e21b196d69ba96a839.jpg
New telescopic Reel

This week I have added more items to get some meat around the game mechanics, and to make the world have more items to discover. 

Here is a list of recently added items:

 Metal parts: Used for crafting items.
 Juniper wood: Obtained by chopping down new juniper trees (model WIP)
 Juniper and wood planks: Crafted by combining tree type in crafting bench.
 Sugar beets and seeds: Can be planted and crafted into sugar which is used for cooking
 Flour and bread: Wheat can now be crafted into flour that can be crafted to bread and croissant
 Cake: Can be cooked on the stove and heals a lot
 Berry jams: Every berry can now be crafted into a jam. These give more health
 Telescopic Reel: Acts like a fishing rob but has more range to catch those deep-sea fish (WIP)
 Different ammo sizes: We added max ammo that can be added to your gun and added 25 and 50 sized ammo boxes
 Snack bar
 Energy drink: Gives you a small amount of energy and a small running speed buff
 Crafting & cooking books: To make it easier for players to know what can and cannot be crafted/cooked I made books that show every item that can be crafted and how to craft them.


Other changes

 Added 10 new achievements
 Added energy symbol on the consumable items inventory icon
 Added item icons for Energy Drink, Flour, Croissant, and Tarp
 Added a slight tilt to the player camera when placing items to make the items easier to place down where you want them
 Re-added caught fish notification
 Removed random rotation when placing a tent. Using restricted rotation instead
 Increased tree health by about 300%
 A few bug fixes
